task.objective: Create the SQLite database plumbing (engine, session factory, declarative Base, get_db dependency), a bare FastAPI application instance with no routes mounted, and a pytest conftest exposing two fixtures - an isolated per-test database session and a TestClient bound to that same session - which every Layer 1, 2 and 4 test will use.

requirements.requirement:
Create `app/database.py` with exactly this content:
"""Database engine, session factory, declarative base and request dependency."""
from collections.abc import Generator from pathlib import Path
from sqlalchemy import create_engine from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Session, sessionmaker
DATABASE_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "link_shelf.db" DATABASE_URL = f"sqlite:///{DATABASE_PATH}"
engine = create_engine( DATABASE_URL, connect_args={"check_same_thread": False}, )
SessionLocal = sessionmaker( bind=engine, class_=Session, autocommit=False, autoflush=False, expire_on_commit=False, )
class Base(DeclarativeBase): """Declarative base class for every Link Shelf model."""
def get_db() -> Generator[Session, None, None]: """Yield a database session and close it when the request finishes.""" db = SessionLocal() try: yield db finally: db.close()
Notes that must be preserved exactly as written above: - `DATABASE_PATH` resolves to `<repository root>/link_shelf.db`, because this module sits at `app/database.py` and `.parent.parent` is the repository root. That filename is the one `.gitignore` already excludes. - `check_same_thread: False` is required because FastAPI serves requests from a threadpool while SQLite's default forbids cross-thread connection use. - `expire_on_commit=False` keeps ORM attributes readable after `commit()`, which every endpoint task needs when it returns the object it just wrote. - Use `class Base(DeclarativeBase)`. Do not use `declarative_base()`; it is the legacy 1.x style. - Do NOT call `Base.metadata.create_all` at import time in this module. L4-001 creates the schema for the running application; the test fixtures create it for tests.

Create `app/main.py` with exactly this content:
"""FastAPI application instance for Link Shelf."""
from fastapi import FastAPI
app = FastAPI( title="Link Shelf", version="0.1.0", description="Store links with an optional title, list them newest first, and tag them.", )
No routers are included and no route functions are defined at this layer. Task L4-001 adds `app.include_router(router)` for the save_link, list_links and tag_links routers and creates the schema at startup. Do not anticipate that work here.

Create `tests/conftest.py` with exactly this content:
"""Shared pytest fixtures: an isolated database session and a client bound to it."""
from collections.abc import Generator
import pytest from fastapi.testclient import TestClient from sqlalchemy import create_engine from sqlalchemy.orm import Session, sessionmaker from sqlalchemy.pool import StaticPool
import app.models # noqa: F401 - registers every model on Base.metadata from app.database import Base, get_db from app.main import app as fastapi_app
@pytest.fixture(name="db_session") def db_session_fixture() -> Generator[Session, None, None]: """Yield a Session on a private in-memory database, empty at the start of each test.""" engine = create_engine( "sqlite://", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False}, poolclass=StaticPool, ) Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine) testing_session_local = sessionmaker( bind=engine, class_=Session, autocommit=False, autoflush=False, expire_on_commit=False, ) session = testing_session_local() try: yield session finally: session.close() engine.dispose()
@pytest.fixture(name="client") def client_fixture(db_session: Session) -> Generator[TestClient, None, None]: """Yield a TestClient whose routes use the same session as the db_session fixture."""
def override_get_db() -> Generator[Session, None, None]: yield db_session
fastapi_app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db try: with TestClient(fastapi_app) as test_client: yield test_client finally: fastapi_app.dependency_overrides.clear()
Notes that must be preserved exactly as written above: - `import app.models` is deliberate and must stay. Layer 1 registers Link, Tag and LinkTag by importing them in `app/models/__init__.py`; without this import, `Base.metadata.create_all` in the fixture would create no tables and every Layer 1 and 2 test would fail with "no such table". The `# noqa: F401` marks it as an intentionally unused import. - `sqlite://` with no path is an in-memory database. `StaticPool` makes every connection from this engine reuse the single in-memory connection, so the tables created by `create_all` are visible to the session and to requests made through the client. - A new engine is built per test, so each test starts from an empty database and nothing leaks between tests. `engine.dispose()` discards it afterwards. - The file-backed `link_shelf.db` is never touched by tests. The fixtures use their own in-memory engine, not `app.database.engine`. - `dependency_overrides` is cleared in a `finally` so a failing test cannot leave the override in place for the next one.

Create `tests/test_setup.py` with exactly this content:
"""Smoke tests for the Layer 0 fixtures."""
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient from sqlalchemy import text from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from app.database import Base, get_db from app.main import app as fastapi_app
def test_db_session_executes_a_query(db_session: Session) -> None: assert db_session.execute(text("SELECT 1")).scalar_one() == 1
def test_db_session_creates_a_leftover_table(db_session: Session) -> None: db_session.execute(text("CREATE TABLE isolation_probe (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)")) db_session.commit() names = set( db_session.execute( text("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table'") ).scalars() ) assert "isolation_probe" in names
def test_each_test_receives_a_fresh_database(db_session: Session) -> None: names = set( db_session.execute( text("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table'") ).scalars() ) assert names == set(Base.metadata.tables)
def test_client_serves_the_application(client: TestClient) -> None: response = client.get("/openapi.json") assert response.status_code == 200 assert response.json()["info"]["title"] == "Link Shelf"
def test_client_overrides_the_database_dependency(client: TestClient) -> None: assert get_db in fastapi_app.dependency_overrides
Notes: - `test_db_session_creates_a_leftover_table` deliberately leaves a table behind, and `test_each_test_receives_a_fresh_database` - which pytest runs next, file order being collection order - asserts the next test's database contains only the tables declared on `Base.metadata`. Together they prove the per-test isolation the later layers rely on. At this layer `Base.metadata.tables` is empty, so the assertion is `names == set()`; once Layer 1 registers models the same assertion still holds without editing. - Do not assert anything about which routes are or are not mounted. L4-001 mounts three routers and must not have to edit this file.

Do NOT create any model module, schema module, router or route. Do NOT edit `app/models/__init__.py`, `pytest.ini`, `.gitignore`, `pyproject.toml` or `requirements.txt`. Do NOT run `git init` and do NOT touch `.git`.

class Base(DeclarativeBase): """Declarative base class for every Link Shelf model."""
Import as: `from app.database import Base` Every model class in `app/models/` must subclass this and set `__tablename__`.

# app/database.py from collections.abc import Generator from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
def get_db() -> Generator[Session, None, None]: """Yield a database session and close it when the request finishes.""" ...
Import as: `from app.database import get_db` Use in a route as: `db: Session = Depends(get_db)` The `client` test fixture overrides this callable, so any route that takes its session this way is automatically wired to the test database.

# app/database.py from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker, Session
SessionLocal: sessionmaker[Session] # bind=engine, class_=Session, autocommit=False, autoflush=False, expire_on_commit=False
Import as: `from app.database import SessionLocal` `expire_on_commit=False` means ORM attributes stay readable after `commit()`.

# app/main.py from fastapi import FastAPI
app = FastAPI( title="Link Shelf", version="0.1.0", description="Store links with an optional title, list them newest first, and tag them.", )
Import as: `from app.main import app` No routers are included at this layer. L4-001 adds `app.include_router(router)` for the save_link, list_links and tag_links routers.

# tests/conftest.py import pytest from collections.abc import Generator from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
@pytest.fixture(name="db_session") def db_session_fixture() -> Generator[Session, None, None]: ...
Fixture name: `db_session`. Scope: function (a new engine and database per test). Yields: a `sqlalchemy.orm.Session` on a private in-memory SQLite database with every table in `Base.metadata` already created.
Use in a test as: def test_something(db_session: Session) -> None: db_session.add(some_model_instance) db_session.commit()
Contract every later test may rely on: - The database is empty at the start of each test and discarded at the end. - Tables are created from `Base.metadata`, which is populated by `import app.models` in conftest.py. A model that is not imported in `app/models/__init__.py` will have no table. - The file-backed `link_shelf.db` is never touched.

# tests/conftest.py import pytest from collections.abc import Generator from fastapi.testclient import TestClient from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
@pytest.fixture(name="client") def client_fixture(db_session: Session) -> Generator[TestClient, None, None]: ...
Fixture name: `client`. Scope: function. Depends on: `db_session`. Yields: a `fastapi.testclient.TestClient` wrapping `app.main.app`, entered as a context manager so startup and shutdown events run.
Contract every later test may rely on: - `app.dependency_overrides[get_db]` yields the SAME Session object the `db_session` fixture yields, so a row written through `db_session` is visible to a request made through `client`, and the reverse. - Requesting both fixtures in one test is supported and gives one shared session: def test_something(client: TestClient, db_session: Session) -> None: ... - The override is cleared after each test, including when the test fails.
